final.summary: Recommended: fused. Peak 90th pct core temp 37.95 °C (limit 38.0), tightest margin 0.04 °C, 63% of priority-weighted work done.
reasons: **Heat is right at the limit.** This plan keeps body temperatures just under the 38 °C safety line, even for the crew members who run hottest. The cushion is tiny (less than a tenth of a degree), so any extra heat, effort, or missed break could push someone over. Stick closely to the planned rest and water breaks.

**We get about two-thirds of the important work done.** Finishing more would mean more heat exposure. One option gets slightly more done (65% instead of 63%), but it brings crew temperatures almost exactly to the limit, leaving no room for error. Another option gets the same amount done as this plan while running a hair cooler.

**Everyone stays indoors from 1:30 to 2:30 PM because of lightning.** The plan works around this break, and it also gives the crew a chance to cool down. Don't try to make up the lost time by pushing harder afterward.
Peak 90th pct core temp 37.95 °C (limit 38.0), tightest margin 0.04 °C, 63% of priority-weighted work done.

Hard safety rules:
- Every worker's 90th percentile core temperature must stay below 38.0 °C all shift. Harder work, sun and high WBGT heat people up; 30-min shade rests cool them down.
- Breaks: at most 3 work slots in a row, then a 'rest' slot; at most 2 in a row if any of those slots has WBGT >= 30.0 °C.
- No outdoor tasks during hazards that stop outdoor work. After lightning, outdoor work stays stopped for 30 more minutes.
- Workers who are not acclimatized never do very_heavy tasks when WBGT >= 28.0 °C.
Validity: one entry per slot per worker; off-site workers rest; skills and allowed slots must match.
